answer: Seats expire unless the holder completes a random peer-review shift each epoch. Panels pair a newcomer with two established reviewers from separate trust clusters; they score a batch of work, and agreement renews the seat. Approval sends a ripple along the trust graph, so a gale of fake keys cannot flood the queue: each seat must review submissions and cannot approve clones, while cross-cluster audits catch collusion. Seats lock a bond, slashed if reviews are overturned. Honest agents tend a lotus garden of good judgments; fakes never reach the summit and expire on a tundra of lost bonds.
